category_title: Jamaican Grade 7 students with multiple literacy failures who transition from 'at-risk' to 'risk-takers' through radio simulation
minimal_context: The student is sitting at the classroom news desk to write a script for a weather report.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please sit at the news desk and write down the script for today's weather report.

STUDENT: (Slouches in the chair) I'm not writing anything. I don't want to read and learn this.

TUTOR: You need to write the script so the newscaster can read it to the audience.

STUDENT: I don't care. I'm not doing it. Every time I take a test I just end up failing again anyway.

TUTOR: Just try your best to write down the headline.

STUDENT: (Knocks the recycled headset off the desk) I said no! I can't even read these words, I failed that Grade 4 test four times already! Leave me alone!

options.A: Assign two to five letters per month for the student to learn and identify at month's end.
options.B: Observe the target behavior during class, recording data in scatter plots and ABC charts.
options.C: Implement relatively tight timelines for the student to complete the weather report script.
options.D: Promote the curriculum as conversations, experiences, and situated social practices rather than standardized approaches.
